skill.name: discord-bot-architect
skill.description: Build and review production-oriented Discord bot architectures using Discord.js v14 and Pycord patterns for commands, intents, components, and rate limits.
skill.summary: Guides Discord bot architecture for Discord.js and Pycord projects.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The reviewed skill is documentation with embedded Discord.js and Pycord examples, not installable executable code. Static findings mostly point to Markdown fences, local module loading examples, and standard environment-token handling; I found no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior.

remediation.issue: Dynamic local module loading is shown without a trust boundary note.
remediation.suggestion: State that command and event folders must be developer-controlled, and validate extension and path before loading modules.

remediation.issue: Token handling examples rely on dotenv without secret management guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to keep .env files out of version control and use platform secret stores in production.

remediation.issue: Several code fences and snippets are malformed or truncated.
remediation.suggestion: Fix duplicated fences and incomplete examples so scanners and users can review the guidance accurately.

content.value_statement: Discord bot projects need correct intents, commands, components, and rate-limit handling. This skill gives architecture patterns for Discord.js and Pycord bots.
actual_capabilities: Shows Discord.js v14 client setup with minimal gateway intents and slash command loading.
Shows Pycord bot setup with slash commands, cogs, and environment token loading.
Provides patterns for buttons, select menus, modals, and component collectors.
Calls out anti-patterns such as message content commands, startup command sync, and blocking work.
Highlights operational concerns for command propagation, invite URLs, modals, and privileged intents.
limitations: Examples are templates and require testing before production use.
Some source snippets are incomplete and may need repair before copying.
It does not provide full hosting, database, CI, or observability setup.
It does not manage Discord developer portal configuration or token rotation.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Bot
use_cases.description: Define a clean Discord.js or Pycord project structure with slash commands, events, and minimal gateway intents.

use_cases.title: Review Bot Architecture
use_cases.description: Check an existing design for risky intents, command sync problems, component handling, and event loop blocking.

use_cases.title: Design Interactive Workflows
use_cases.description: Create button, select menu, and modal flows that match Discord interaction timing rules.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Bot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use discord-bot-architect to design a Discord.js v14 starter bot with slash commands, minimal gateway intents, and a safe folder structure. Include setup steps and files to create.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Message Commands
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Discord bot plan and replace prefix message commands with slash commands where possible. Explain which gateway intents are still required and why.

prompt_templates.title: Add Interactive Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Discord interaction flow that uses buttons, select menus, and modals. Include timing constraints, authorization checks, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Scaling
prompt_templates.prompt: Architect a production Discord bot for a large server network. Cover sharding, rate limits, deployment, secret handling, command registration, and observability.

output_examples.input: Plan a Discord.js moderation bot with slash commands.
output_examples.output: A concise architecture with client setup, command modules, required intents, permission checks, deployment guidance, and rate-limit notes.

output_examples.input: Review my Pycord bot design for production risks.
output_examples.output: A review covering privileged intents, command sync strategy, cogs, token storage, blocking operations, and interaction response timing.

output_examples.input: Design an interactive role menu for a community server.
output_examples.output: A component plan with select menu options, button actions, user authorization, timeout behavior, and follow-up response handling.

best_practices: Enable only required gateway intents and avoid Message Content unless required.
Deploy slash commands separately from runtime startup to reduce rate-limit risk.
Store bot tokens in managed secrets and rotate them after exposure.
anti_patterns: Building new features around prefix commands that require privileged message content.
Syncing global commands every time the bot starts.
Running blocking work inside gateway event handlers.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete Discord bot?
faq.answer: It provides architecture guidance and patterns. You still need to implement, test, and deploy the bot.

faq.question: Does it support both JavaScript and Python?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Discord.js v14 for JavaScript and Pycord for Python.

faq.question: Can it help with slash commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on slash command structure, registration concerns, and interaction handling.

faq.question: Does it require Message Content intent?
faq.answer: No. The guidance recommends avoiding Message Content unless the bot truly needs it.

faq.question: Can it handle production scaling?
faq.answer: It can guide planning for sharding, rate limits, and command deployment. It does not operate infrastructure for you.

faq.question: Is the source ready to copy without changes?
faq.answer: No. Some examples are incomplete and should be reviewed, repaired, and tested before use.
